results.title: ℤ is Diophantine in ℚ
results.summary: A new manuscript reports one polynomial equation that separates the integers from all other fractions.
results.status: Posted 5 November 2026. AI reviews only. The Lean proof is incomplete.

results.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis
results.summary: Two groups report an algorithm that solves 3-SAT faster than every exponential time, but only for enormous inputs.
results.status: Posted 26 October 2026 by two groups. Two separate Lean proofs. Expert review continues.

results.title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
results.summary: OpenAI reports that no zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part above 7/8. This limit controls the error in prime counts.
results.status: Posted 6 October 2026. Lean proof of the 7/8 bound. Experts who studied the proof largely agree that it is correct.

results.title: The Kakeya conjecture in every dimension
results.summary: OpenAI reports that a set with a unit segment in every direction always has full dimension, even when its volume is zero.
results.status: Posted 26 October 2026. Lean proof. No published human check found.

results.title: The Jacobian conjecture is false
results.summary: A polynomial map in three variables can preserve volume at every point and still send three points to one.
results.status: Posted 19 July 2026. Anyone can check the example by direct calculation. The two-variable case remains open.

results.title: Erdős's unit distance problem
results.summary: The number of pairs at distance 1 among n points can exceed what Erdős expected. A later report also lowers the upper limit.
results.status: Lower bound, May 2026: checked by outside mathematicians. Upper bound, October 2026: Lean proof.

results.title: Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ
results.summary: OpenAI reports that no algorithm can decide if every polynomial equation has a solution in fractions.
results.status: Posted 6 October 2026. No Lean proof. Later papers build on it. No published independent check found.

results.title: The Unique Games Conjecture
results.summary: OpenAI reports a proof that some systems of two-variable equations are hard to satisfy even approximately. Many approximation algorithms are then the best possible unless P = NP.
results.status: Posted 6 October 2026. Lean proof. Experts are studying the proof and giving talks on it.

results.title: Navier–Stokes blow-up
results.summary: OpenAI reports that a smooth force on a fluid at rest can produce infinite speed in finite time. The case with no force remains open.
results.status: Posted 8 September 2026. Lean proof. The Clay Mathematics Institute calls the problem apparently settled, and its review continues.
